label: Recipe API
title: Creating recipes
lead: Wanna make a super secret item? Have it require 500 INT to craft, so that only blueprints can reveal it.
bodyHtml:
RecipeRegistry.Register

CUCoreLib registers normal vanilla Recipe objects. The recipe uses the game's existing crafting visibility, ingredient matching, item consumption, and result spawning flow.

Recipe visibility follows vanilla rules: if specialKnown is false, the recipe only appears when the player's INT is at least INT - 3. Keep early test recipes low, such as INT = 10, or they can look like they failed to register.

RecipeRegistry.Register(new Recipe
{
    INT = 6,
    result = new RecipeResult { id = "cinderstalkbag", amount = 1 },
    items = new List<RecipeItem>
    {
        new RecipeItem { specificId = "cinderstalk", minimumCondition = 0.9f },
        new RecipeItem { specificId = "cinderstalk", minimumCondition = 0.9f },
        new RecipeItem { specificId = "cinderstalk", minimumCondition = 0.9f },
        new RecipeItem { specificId = "rope", minimumCondition = 0f },
        new RecipeItem { specificId = "charredfern", minimumCondition = 0.9f },
        new RecipeItem { specificId = "plasticchunk", minimumCondition = 0.9f }
    },
    category = Recipes.RecipeCategory.Utilities
});

Ingredients

A RecipeItem can require a specific ID or a crafting quality. Specific IDs are best when you need exactly water, rope, or one of your custom item IDs. Qualities are best for reusable tools or broad food/material groups.

For liquids, the constructor value is mL. For normal items, it is minimum condition.

Fields

A recipe is made from three vanilla game objects: Recipe, RecipeResult, and RecipeItem. CUCoreLib registers those normal objects directly, so the fields below are the ones the game actually uses while matching ingredients, showing the crafting UI, and spawning the result.

CUCoreLib also normalizes one common vanilla quirk: if you set specificId, it automatically treats that ingredient as specific = true, and if you leave the default minimumCondition = 0.9f on a specific ingredient it rewrites it to 0f so exact-item recipes do not accidentally require 90% condition.

Field Type What it controls
Recipe.specialKnownboolIf true, the recipe is always visible. If false, vanilla only shows it when the player's INT is at least INT - 3.
Recipe.INTintIntelligence requirement for crafting. Vanilla can reduce output quality or fail the craft when the player is below this value.
Recipe.itemsList<RecipeItem>The ingredient list. Each entry describes one required item, tool, or liquid input.
Recipe.resultRecipeResultThe output object the recipe produces. This contains the result ID, amount, liquid flag, and starting condition/volume.
Recipe.categoryRecipes.RecipeCategoryCrafting-menu category only. Use one of Materials, Tools, Medicine, Utilities, or Food.
Recipe.isRepairboolMarks the recipe as a repair recipe. CUCoreLib uses this to avoid the normal self-ignore behavior for result IDs when matching ingredients.
RecipeResult.idstringThe item ID or liquid ID produced by the recipe. This is required.
RecipeResult.isLiquidboolWhether id points to a liquid registration instead of an item prefab. Liquid results spawn into a container and treat resultCondition as mL.
RecipeResult.amountintHow many results the craft produces. For non-liquid items, values above 1 spawn multiple items.
RecipeResult.resultConditionfloatStarting condition for item results, usually from 0 to 1. For liquid results, this is the output volume in mL.
RecipeResult.dontDrainResultLiquidboolOnly matters when the crafted item is a liquid container. If false, vanilla clears the container contents after spawning it. Set it to true when your crafted item should keep its starting liquid.
RecipeItem.specificboolWhether this ingredient requires one exact ID instead of matching by crafting quality. CUCoreLib sets this automatically when specificId is filled.
RecipeItem.specificIdstringThe exact item ID or liquid ID required when specific is enabled.
RecipeItem.isLiquidboolWhether this ingredient consumes liquid from a container instead of using a normal item instance.
RecipeItem.qualityCraftingQualityQuality-based ingredient requirement. Use this when any item or liquid with the right crafting quality should satisfy the slot.
RecipeItem.minimumConditionfloatFor specific items, the minimum condition required. For quality-based items, the amount of condition/tool-use consumed. For liquids, this is the required or consumed volume in mL.
RecipeItem.destroyItemboolWhether crafting destroys the matched item after use. Set it to false for reusable tools such as knives, hammers, or other quality providers that should only lose condition.

Tip: use specificId for exact ingredients, and quality plus destroyItem = false for reusable tools.
